roastingCycles.title: First Cycle — Bamboo Packing & Clay Seal
roastingCycles.description: Natural sea salt is densely packed into thick mountain bamboo stalks and sealed on both open ends with pure yellow clay.

roastingCycles.title: Second Cycle — Bamboo Sap Fusion
roastingCycles.description: Fired over natural pine firewood. As the bamboo tube burns, its essential resin and sap infuse the salt.

roastingCycles.title: Third Cycle — Thermal Consolidation
roastingCycles.description: The cylindrical salt pillar is ground, packed into fresh green bamboo stalks with fresh clay, and re-fired.

roastingCycles.title: Fourth Cycle — Mineral Migration
roastingCycles.description: Sustained heat drives natural clay minerals deep into the salt matrix, evening out the mineral balance.

roastingCycles.title: Fifth Cycle — The Colour Shift
roastingCycles.description: The crystals soften in harshness, taking on a subtle smoky note and beginning their natural color shift.

roastingCycles.title: Sixth Cycle — Deep Roasting Integration
roastingCycles.description: Bamboo fibers and kiln heat integrate fully with the salt crystals under sustained kiln temperatures.

roastingCycles.title: Seventh Cycle — High-Heat Cleansing
roastingCycles.description: High temperatures cleanse the salt, eliminating raw moisture and environmental impurities.

roastingCycles.title: Eighth Cycle — Pre-Transformation
roastingCycles.description: The glowing red salt pillars consolidate under pine firewood fire, preparing for molten fusion.

roastingCycles.title: Ninth Cycle — Molten Bamboo Fusion
roastingCycles.description: At peak pine fire temperature, the salt melts and fuses into rich brownish-violet crystals with a delicate smoky umami finish.

timelineStages.title: Bamboo Selection & Hand-Packing
timelineStages.description: Thick-walled mountain bamboo stalks rich in sap are harvested, cut into natural firing tubes, packed tightly with solar sea salt, and capped with mineral yellow clay.

timelineStages.title: Low-Roasting Sap Infusion (Cycles 1 – 3)
timelineStages.description: Fired over resin-rich pine firewood between 800°C and 950°C. Essential bamboo resins and sap vaporize directly into the salt core.

timelineStages.title: Mineral Migration (Cycles 4 – 6)
timelineStages.description: Hardened salt pillars are ground, packed into fresh green bamboo tubes with fresh yellow clay, and fired between 1,000°C and 1,100°C to integrate clay minerals.

timelineStages.title: High-Heat Thermal Cleansing (Cycles 7 – 8)
timelineStages.description: Fired at 1,200°C–1,300°C. High thermal energy cleanses the salt, expelling raw bitterness and environmental microplastics.

timelineStages.title: Peak Molten Fusion (Cycle 9)
timelineStages.description: At 1,500°C+, the salt liquifies into molten lava, fusing minerals, bamboo sap, and clay into dense brownish-violet crystal boulders that are finely granulated.

costJustification.headline: Why does 9x bamboo salt cost more?
costJustification.tagline: Each batch takes 21 days and nine firings, and much of the salt is lost in the process.
points: 21 days of continuous kiln monitoring by artisanal salt masters
9 separate fresh bamboo stalks and fresh yellow clay seals per batch
High yield loss during successive firings at 1,500°C
